v.why: Filling the empty direct input-to-output edge adds a missing path and gave large gains (exps 72, 75-78), while replacing an existing op on edge 3 was roughly neutral or harmful (71, 73, 74).
Adding a residual shortcut where none exists typically helps far more (exps 11, 15, 18, 19) than swapping out an existing op on edge 3 (12-14, 20).
With edge 4 absent, removing edge 5 cuts every deep path into the output, which was catastrophic in exps 63-64.
When edge 4 is already pooling, node 1 reaches the output only through two parameter-free pools, so losing the conv on edge 0 hurts much more (exps 87, 89).
If edge 5 is absent, edge 4 is the only learned path into the output, so turning it into a pool removes the remaining output-side conv (exp 48).
Pooling on edge 4 only adds a path when it replaces 'none', but replaces a conv otherwise (exps 43, 46 vs 41, 44).
With edge 0 absent, edge 1 is the only route from the input into the deep part of the cell, so removing it is much more damaging (exp 27).
Without the input-to-output edge, the network relies entirely on the deep conv chain, so replacing the conv on edge 2 with a skip costs much more (exp 59).
Removing a parameter-free skip on edge 5 loses little compared with removing a conv on edge 5 (exp 65 vs 61, 67, 70).
Upgrading an existing 1x1 conv to 3x3 adds little capacity, compared with replacing none, pool or skip (exp 3 vs 1, 2, 4).

I chose these 10 from the 100 experiments and the cell's DAG structure. Three patterns explain most of them:

- **Edge 3 is the 0→3 path into the output.** When it is `none`, the output relies on deeper paths through nodes 1 and 2. Edits that restore that direct path gain a lot, and edits that make the deeper paths worse lose more, especially on ImageNet16-120.
- **Edges 4 and 5 feed the output.** If one of them is already `none`, removing or weakening the other can disconnect or degrade the output. This produced several drops of 6 to 76 points.
- **Two pooling edges on one path compound.** Adding `avg_pool` on edge 0 hurts much more when edge 4 is already `avg_pool`, because node 1 then reaches the output only through two pools.

Some of these rest on only one or two experiments, so they are less certain than the edge 3 ones:

- Edge 1 → `none` when edge 0 is `none` rests on experiment 27.
- Edge 4 → `avg_pool` when edge 5 is `none` rests on experiment 48.
- Edge 5 → `nor_conv_3x3` when edge 5 is `nor_conv_1x1` rests on experiment 3.
- Edge 5 → `none` when edge 5 is `skip_connect` rests on experiment 65.
